The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City

Inglewood, California
  March 19, 2024

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
March 19, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

MAYOR PRO TEM APPOINTMENT. It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and
seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby appoint Council
Member Morales as Mayor Pro Tem. The motion was carried by the following roll call
vote:
Ayes: Council Member Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
Noes: None; and
Absent: Mayor Butts and Council Member Gray.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem /Successor Agency Chairman Pro
  Tem/Housing Authority Chairman Pro Tem/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Pro Tem Morales, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts, and
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/Joint Powers Authority Member Gray.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel
present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
Authority.

Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member/ Joint Powers
Authority Member Gray arrived at the dais at the hour of 2:01 p.m.

Chairman Pro Tem/Housing Authority Chairman Pro Tem/ Joint Powers Authority
Chairman Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to
address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority

 March 19, 2024

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated March 14, 2024,
  in the amount of $2,738,467.54, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem/Successor Agency Chairman Pro
  Tem/Housing Authority Chairman Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on January 9, 2024, be approved.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Javon Alston for alleged vehicle damage; fallen tree branch on August 7, 2023.
  2. Treneatra Farmer for alleged tire damage; pothole on February 12, 2024.
  3. Ulysess Kinard for alleged personal injury; shot by unknown assailants on October 7,
  2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-3. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 24-156 APPROVED – ELLISON WILSON ADVOCACY, LLC.
  Staff report dated March 19, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members approve a new three-year agreement with Ellison Wilson Advocacy,
  LLC, to provide legislative advocacy services for the City of Inglewood.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 24-156 in an annual amount not to exceed
  $63,000 (total contract amount not to exceed $189,000). The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 24-40 ADOPTED – APPOINTMENTS TO THE SOUTH BAY
  WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB) RATIFIED. Staff report dated
  March 19, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  approve Amendment No. 1 to the Welfare-to-Work Vocational and Direct Services Contract
  by and between the County of Los Angeles and the City of Inglewood, which serves as the
  Administrative Entity for the South Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB).

  2
 March 19, 2024

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby: 1) Make appointments; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-40
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, RATIFYING APPOINTMENTS MADE TO THE SOUTH BAY
  WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD BY ITS MEMBERS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

101  COLLABORATIVE FELLOWSHIP AGREEMENT NO. 24-157 APPROVED –
  LELAND STANFORD JUNIOR UNIVERSITY (STANFORD); RESOLUTION NO.
  24-41 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 OPERATING
  BUDGET. Staff report dated March 19, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor
  and Council Members approve a Collaborative Fellowship Agreement with Leland Stanford
  Junior University (Stanford) on behalf of its Stanford Impact Labs (SIL), for a fellowship
  in the amount of $50,000 to the City of Inglewood for a project entitled Evidence for Policy
  Fellowship, under the Direction of Qiuana Williams.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Collaborative Fellowship Agreement No. 24-157;
  and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-41 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, ACCEPTING A GRANT AWARD OF $50,000 FROM
  STANFORD UNIVERSITY FOR A COLLABORATIVE FELLOWSHIP
  AGREEMENT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

171  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – IT’S YOUR PARTY FLORAL & EVENT DESIGN
  (IT’S YOUR PARTY). Staff report dated March 19, 2024, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members authorize payment of two (2) invoices submitted by
  It’s Your Party Floral & Event Design (It’s Your Party), for providing material and labor
  for the City’s Senior Center Christmas events and Black History Celebration.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $5,700. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – TSM RECOVERY & RECYCLING CO. INC (TSM).
  Staff report dated March 19, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members authorize payment of three (3) invoices submitted by TSM Recovery &
  Recycling Co. Inc. (TSM) for collection of medical and hazardous waste.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $740.10. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

  3
 March 19, 2024

126  REPORTS—CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson wished Christine Padilla,
  the Management Assistant in the City Clerk’s Office, a happy birthday.

126  MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated March 19, 2024, was
  presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the Month ending January 31,
  2024.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales ordered the report received and filed.

  Council Member Faulk left the dais at the hour of 2:05 p.m.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Isaac Abdu Hawk, spoke concerning his wonderful experience since joining the Inglewood
  Little League in the 13 and under category. He mentioned the number of attendees on
  opening day and the fantastic facilities. Mr. Hawk also mentioned how people from other
  cities marveled at the fields as they played. He stated that you could tell that the people who
  put it together worked hard and cared. He discussed data from the California Department of
  Education website and compared it to the percentage of kids that played in the Little League.
  Mr. Hawk also discussed the absence of black coaches and other cities' ability to use the
  playing field, which he felt was a problem. Finally, he explained what happened when he
  questioned the absence of black coaches and the answer received.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning an accommodation received from the City
  of Inglewood working with the Inglewood Police Department. She stated that she
  experienced something two months ago with her grandson, who was 16 years old, a
  straight-A student, and a basketball player, which spoke volumes. She mentioned being at
  the 76th and Arbor Vitae gas station and sent her grandson to the gas station with a
  hundred-dollar bill to pay for gas. She also stated that her grandson returned to the car
  and said they wouldn’t exchange it for him, and he couldn’t get gas. The speaker also
  mentioned the number of vehicles at the gas station and how she walked inside to wait in
  line. She described a Caucasian man entering the gas station with a hundred-dollar bill to pay for
  lottery tickets. She explained that she asked the other customers if she could  proceed to the
  front to speak to the cashier. The speaker added that the cashier told her she had to get change
  from another drawer and addressed her grandson as that boy.  Finally, she added that she
  believed something was happening and should be addressed.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Pro Tem Morales declared the
  meeting adjourned in memory of Guadalupe Cornejo, at the hour of 2:24 p.m.

  Approved this 30th day of April, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ____________________________
  Eloy Morales, Jr., Mayor Pro Tem
